name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q01 - Morphology and behavioral adaptations of frog overview

questiontext.text:
Consider the following statements regarding the structural organisation of animals:

Statement I: The most common species of frog found in India is Rana tigrina.

Statement II: Frogs are poikilothermic animals whose internal temperature fluctuates with the environment.

Statement III: The body of an adult frog is divided into head, neck, and trunk.

Statement IV: Frogs never drink water through their mouth but absorb it directly through the skin.

Statement V: Adult frogs possess an elongated muscular tail that propels them during swimming.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Species and Poikilothermy
The common Indian bullfrog is taxonomically identified as Rana tigrina, belonging to class Amphibia. As cold-blooded poikilotherms, frogs lack homeostatic thermal regulation. Thus, both the first and second statements are factually accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of Body Segmentation
The streamlined body of an adult frog consists solely of head and trunk; both a neck and tail are completely absent in the adult stage. Thus, the third and fifth statements are factually false.

Step 3: Evaluation of Cutaneous Water Absorption
Frogs do not ingest liquid water orally; instead, their vascularized, mucous-coated skin osmotically absorbs ambient moisture. Thus, the fourth statement is factually accurate.

Step 4: Final Conceptual Conclusion
Statements I, II, and IV are correct, whereas Statements III and V are incorrect.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II and Statement IV only
Statement I, Statement III and Statement V only
Statement II, Statement III and Statement IV only
Statement I, Statement II, Statement III and Statement IV

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q02 - Digestive tract anatomy and duodenal secretions

questiontext.text:
Consider the following statements regarding the structural organisation of animals:

Statement I: The alimentary canal of the frog is short because frogs are carnivores.

Statement II: Prey is captured using an anteriorly attached, bilobed muscular tongue.

Statement III: Digestion in the stomach involves HCl and gastric juices converting food into chyme.

Statement IV: Bile contains proteolytic enzymes that digest proteins into polypeptides.

Statement V: Final digestion and absorption of nutrients take place in the intestine across villi.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Gut Length and Ingestion
Adult frogs feed on animal prey, which digests rapidly without requiring prolonged gut transit, reducing intestinal length. Prey is captured using the bilobed tongue. Thus, the first and second statements are factually accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of Gastric Breakdown
The glandular stomach wall secretes hydrochloric acid and gastric enzymes to digest food into an acidic pulp called chyme. Thus, the third statement is factually accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of Bile Components
Bile contains bile salts that emulsify fats; it completely lacks digestive enzymes. Thus, the fourth statement claiming proteolytic enzymes in bile is factually false.

Step 4: Evaluation of Intestinal Absorption
Final enzymatic digestion and mucosal nutrient absorption occur in the small intestine across microscopic folds called villi and microvilli. Thus, the fifth statement is factually accurate.

Step 5: Final Conceptual Conclusion
Statements I, II, III, and V are correct, whereas Statement IV is incorrect.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II and Statement IV only
Statement I, Statement II, Statement III and Statement V only
Statement II, Statement III and Statement IV only
Statement I, Statement III, Statement IV and Statement V only

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q03 - Circulatory components and cardiac accessory chambers

questiontext.text:
Consider the following statements regarding the structural organisation of animals:

Statement I: The heart of an adult frog consists of three chambers: two atria and one ventricle.

Statement II: Sinus venosus is a triangular structure that joins the right atrium and receives blood from venae cavae.

Statement III: The ventricle opens into a sac-like conus arteriosus on the ventral surface.

Statement IV: Erythrocytes of frog blood are nucleated and contain hemoglobin.

Statement V: Lymph in frogs contains a much higher concentration of erythrocytes than whole blood.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Heart Chambers and Outflow
The frog heart has three internal chambers: right atrium, left atrium, and a single muscular ventricle. Blood leaves the ventricle via the ventral conus arteriosus. Thus, the first and third statements are factually accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of Sinus Venosus
The thin-walled triangular sinus venosus joins the right atrium dorsally to receive systemic venous blood from the major venae cavae. Thus, the second statement is factually accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of Blood and Lymph Cytology
Erythrocytes in frog blood are nucleated, biconvex, and contain hemoglobin. In contrast, lymph is a filtered transudate that completely lacks red blood cells. Thus, the fourth statement is factually accurate, while the fifth statement is factually false.

Step 4: Final Conceptual Conclusion
Statements I, II, III, and IV are correct, whereas Statement V is incorrect.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II and Statement V only
Statement II, Statement III and Statement V only
Statement I, Statement II, Statement III and Statement IV only
Statement I, Statement II, Statement III, Statement IV and Statement V

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q04 - Terrestrial and aquatic respiratory organ specializations

questiontext.text:
Consider the following statements regarding the structural organisation of animals:

Statement I: In water, skin acts as an aquatic respiratory organ by cutaneous diffusion of dissolved oxygen.

Statement II: On land, the buccal cavity, skin, and lungs can all act as respiratory organs.

Statement III: The lungs are a pair of elongated, pink-coloured, sac-like structures in the thorax.

Statement IV: During aestivation and hibernation, gaseous exchange takes place exclusively through the skin.

Statement V: Air inspired through the nostrils enters the buccal cavity before reaching the lungs.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Cutaneous Respiration
When submerged in water, oxygen exchange is achieved across the moist, vascularized skin by diffusion. Furthermore, during seasonal dormancy (aestivation and hibernation), skin respiration is the sole route of gas exchange. Thus, the first and fourth statements are factually accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of Terrestrial Respiratory Routes
On land, frogs respire through three active surfaces: the mucous lining of the buccal cavity, the skin, and a pair of lungs. Thus, the second statement is factually accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of Pulmonary Anatomy and Airway Path
The lungs are paired, elongated, pink sac-like structures located in the thorax. Air enters through the external nostrils into the buccal cavity, which pumps air into the lungs. Thus, the third and fifth statements are factually accurate.

Step 4: Final Conceptual Conclusion
All five statements (Statements I, II, III, IV, and V) are correct.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II and Statement III only
Statement II, Statement III and Statement IV only
Statement I, Statement III, Statement IV and Statement V only
Statement I, Statement II, Statement III, Statement IV and Statement V

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q05 - Male urinogenital ductwork and Bidder canal

questiontext.text:
Consider the following statements regarding the structural organisation of animals:

Statement I: Testes in male frogs are attached to the kidneys by a double fold of peritoneum called mesorchium.

Statement II: Vasa efferentia, 10 to 12 in number, emerge from the testes and open into Bidder's canal in the kidneys.

Statement III: In male frogs, the ureters act as urinogenital ducts communicating with the cloaca.

Statement IV: In female frogs, the ovaries communicate directly with the renal tubules through Bidder's canal.

Statement V: The cloaca is a common median chamber that passes faecal matter, urine, and sperms to the exterior.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Testicular Anchorage and Ductwork
The male testes are adhered to the kidneys by the peritoneal mesorchium. From each testis, 10 to 12 vasa efferentia enter the kidney and communicate with Bidder's canal. Thus, the first and second statements are factually accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of Urinogenital Ducts and Cloaca
Bidder's canal empties into the ureters, which function as combined urinogenital ducts discharging into the cloaca. The cloaca conveys digestive, excretory, and reproductive products to the exterior. Thus, the third and fifth statements are factually accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of Ovarian-Renal Independence
In female frogs, ovaries maintain no anatomical or functional connection with the kidneys; Bidder's canal and vasa efferentia are entirely absent in females. Thus, the fourth statement is factually false.

Step 4: Final Conceptual Conclusion
Statements I, II, III, and V are correct, whereas Statement IV is incorrect.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II, Statement III and Statement V only
Statement I, Statement II and Statement IV only
Statement II, Statement III and Statement IV only
Statement I, Statement III, Statement IV and Statement V only

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MCQ_Q06 - Female reproductive organs and metamorphosis stages

questiontext.text:
Consider the following statements regarding the structural organisation of animals:

Statement I: A pair of ovaries are situated near the kidneys with no functional connection between them.

Statement II: A pair of oviducts arising from the ovaries open separately and independently into the cloaca.

Statement III: A mature female frog can lay approximately 2500 to 3000 ova at a time.

Statement IV: Fertilisation is internal, occurring inside the female oviducts before egg laying.

Statement V: Development involves an aquatic larval stage called tadpole that undergoes metamorphosis to form the adult.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Ovarian Topography and Oviducts
Female ovaries lie near the kidneys without any functional link; their paired oviducts open separately into the cloaca. Thus, the first and second statements are factually accurate.

Step 2: Evaluation of Fecundity
During oviposition, a mature female lays between 2500 and 3000 ova into the water. Thus, the third statement is factually accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of Fertilisation Environment
Fertilisation in frogs is external, taking place in water during amplexus; it is not internal. Thus, the fourth statement is factually false.

Step 4: Evaluation of Larval Development and Metamorphosis
The fertilized eggs develop into free-swimming, gill-bearing tadpoles, which metamorphose into adult frogs. Thus, the fifth statement is factually accurate.

Step 5: Final Conceptual Conclusion
Statements I, II, III, and V are correct, whereas Statement IV is incorrect.

answer.text: Statement I, Statement II and Statement IV only
Statement I, Statement II, Statement III and Statement V only
Statement II, Statement III and Statement IV only
Statement I, Statement III, Statement IV and Statement V only
